newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says over 500,000 still stranded in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: France says over 500,000 still stranded in Zaire.

text.p: A senior French official said on Friday that hundreds of thousands of refugees remained stranded in eastern Zaire in urgent need of international assistance.

Xavier Emmanuelli, secretary of state for urgent humanitarian action, said reconaissance flights by French aid officials "confirmed the presence of 500,000 to 600,000 refugees or displaced persons in eastern Zaire, divided into several groups".
"They remind us of the urgent need for food and medicine and the possibility of meeting these needs by air," he added in a printed statement.
Long after other nations have given up on the idea, France has argued for an international military mission to the region to help channel aid to the refugees.
The crisis was generated by a rebel advance in eastern Zaire which dislocated hundreds of thousands of people who had fled into Zaire from Rwanda, Burundi and Tanzania.
Emmanuelli said those in direst need included some 100,000 people camped seven km (four miles) outside the village of Lubutu, eastern Zaire.
He said these refugees, hiding in deep forest adjacent to an airfield, had already walked 700 km (more than 400 miles) and were "cruelly in need of food".
Another large group of refugees was found, "extremely tired and in distress" on the road from Kindu to Kisangani, he said.
